fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the entry point, especially at night.
• Trim tree branches and shrubs along the access drive to maintain clearance for fire apparatus and ambulances along the full length of the driveway.
• Clear vegetation from both sides of the access drive to widen the usable travel width for large emergency vehicles.
• Designate and mark a turnaround area near the residence so arriving crews do not have to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Thin dense vegetation between the access drive and the detached structure so responders can reach that building without navigating through heavy brush.
• Post a visible property map or address placard near the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of debris, fallen branches, and overgrowth that could slow or block emergency vehicle movement.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Long Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang over or touch the house.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between them.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the house.
• Cut back ground vegetation along both sides of the driveway so it stays passable.
• Trim any tree branches that hang low over the driveway to keep the full width and height open.
• Keep the area beneath scattered trees clear of dead leaves, dry grass, and loose plant material.
• Thin shrubs growing beneath tree canopies so fire cannot climb from the ground into the trees.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around any outbuildings or secondary structures on the property.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the main road, given the single access point.
• Keep the single access route free of parked vehicles, fallen branches, and overgrown vegetation at all times.
